ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, two downward rays are emitted from vertex O, forming a very small angle α. Points A1 and A3 are on the right ray, and point A2 is on the left ray. The broken line connects back and forth between the two rays in the order OA1, A1A2, A2A3, ..., and these line segments have equal length. Reasoning: Let the length of all line segments be L, and let rn = OAn, that is, the distance from An to O along the ray it is on. A0 = O, so r1 = L. For triangle O A(n−1) An, the angle at O is α, and A(n−1)An = L. By the law of cosines and taking the new intersection point that does not return to the old point, the recurrence solution rn/L = sin(nα)/sin α can be obtained. In order not to intersect, the order of the endpoints of the line segments connecting the two rays cannot be reversed; therefore r1, r3, r5, ... on the right ray must increase, and r2, r4, r6, ... on the left ray must also increase. Now α = 7°. The odd terms on the right up to r13 correspond to angles 7°, 21°, 35°, 49°, 63°, 77°, 91°, and the sine values are still increasing; the even terms on the left up to r12 correspond to angles 14°, 28°, 42°, 56°, 70°, 84°, and the sine values are also increasing. Therefore it can be drawn up to the 13th line segment. But if the 14th line segment is drawn again, then r14 is proportional to sin(98°)=sin(82°), while r12 is proportional to sin(84°), so r14 < r12. The order of the left-side endpoints is reversed, while on the right side r13 > r11, so the new line segment A13A14 will intersect an earlier line segment. Therefore at most 13 line segments can be drawn.

method.method_draft: Use an analytic coordinate/trigonometric route. From the image, read that two rays from O form a narrow angle α, with A1, A3, ... on the right ray and A2, A4, ... on the left ray, and the drawn segments zigzag between the two rays. From the text, take α = 7° and all consecutive segments OA1, A1A2, A2A3, ... to have the same length L. Let r_n = OA_n measured along the appropriate ray, with A_0 = O and r_1 = L. In triangle O A_{n-1} A_n, the included angle at O between the two rays is α, and the side A_{n-1}A_n has length L, so by the law of cosines or law of sines one obtains inductively r_n/L = sin(nα)/sin α for the noncrossing forward choice. Now use the bridge rule that two chords joining opposite sides of an angle cross exactly when the order of their endpoints along the two rays is reversed. Therefore the same-parity sequences r_1, r_3, r_5, ... on the right ray and r_2, r_4, r_6, ... on the left ray must remain increasing. With α = 7°, the right-side sequence is increasing through r_13 because sin 7°, sin 21°, ..., sin 91° increases, and the left-side sequence is increasing through r_12 because sin 14°, ..., sin 84° increases. But r_14 is proportional to sin 98° = sin 82°, which is less than r_12 proportional to sin 84°, so the next segment would reverse the endpoint order and cross an earlier segment. Thus the maximum number of segments is 13.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中从顶点 O 发出两条向下的射线，形成一个很小的夹角 α。点 A1、A3 位于右侧射线上，点 A2 位于左侧射线上，折线按 OA1、A1A2、A2A3、…… 的顺序在两条射线之间来回连接，且这些线段等长。推理：设所有线段长度为 L，并设 rn = OAn，即 An 到 O 沿所在射线的距离，A0 = O，所以 r1 = L。对于三角形 O A(n−1) An，O 处夹角为 α，且 A(n−1)An = L。由余弦定理并取不回到旧点的那个新交点，可得递推解 rn/L = sin(nα)/sin α。为了不相交，连接两条射线的线段的端点顺序不能反转；因此同在右射线上的 r1, r3, r5, ... 必须递增，同在左射线上的 r2, r4, r6, ... 也必须递增。现在 α = 7°。右侧奇数项到 r13 对应角度 7°, 21°, 35°, 49°, 63°, 77°, 91°，正弦值仍递增；左侧偶数项到 r12 对应角度 14°, 28°, 42°, 56°, 70°, 84°，正弦值也递增。因此可以画到第 13 条线段。但若再画第 14 条，则 r14 与 sin(98°)=sin(82°) 成正比，而 r12 与 sin(84°) 成正比，所以 r14 < r12。左侧端点顺序反转，而右侧 r13 > r11，于是新线段 A13A14 会与较早的线段相交。因此最多能画 13 条线段。

method.method_draft: Use a synthetic angle-chasing route. From the image, observe that each new segment alternates from one side of the angle to the other, so every pair of consecutive equal segments forms an isosceles triangle: OA1A2, then A1A2A3, then A2A3A4, and so on. From the text, all consecutive segments have the same length, so each such triangle has two equal sides. In the first triangle OA1A2, the base angle at O is α, so the other base angle is also α. Because the side rays are straight lines, when passing to the next isosceles triangle, the relevant base angle increases by α. Inductively, the triangle formed when drawing the kth segment has base angles (k-1)α and apex angle 180° - 2(k-1)α. For the construction to continue in the same nonintersecting zigzag direction, this apex angle must remain positive, equivalently (k-1)α < 90°. With α = 7°, this gives k - 1 < 90/7, so k ≤ 13. The 13th segment corresponds to base angles 12·7° = 84°, which is possible, while the 14th would require base angles 13·7° = 91°, impossible for the same outward noncrossing triangle and hence would force an intersection/turnback. Therefore the maximum number of lines is 13.

Reasoning: Since all segments have the same length, each pair of consecutive segments forms an isosceles triangle: OA1A2, then A1A2A3, then A2A3A4, and so on. In the first triangle, the angle at O is alpha = 7°, so the other base angle is also 7°. By the same isosceles-triangle angle chase, each new step increases the relevant base angle by alpha. Inductively, when the kth segment is drawn, the relevant base angle is (k-1)alpha, so the apex angle is 180° - 2(k-1)alpha. For the zigzag to keep going without self-intersection, this apex angle must stay positive, i.e. (k-1)alpha < 90°. With alpha = 7°, we get k - 1 < 90/7, so k <= 13. Thus 13 segments can be drawn, while the 14th would require 13*7° = 91° and would force a turnback/intersection.
